G1401.def:
δοῦλος, -η, -ον,
[in LXX, ὁ δ. nearly always for עֶבֶד; ὁ δ. chiefly for שִׁפְחָה ,אָמָה ;]
__1. in bondage to, subject to: Rm 6:19.
__2. As subst., ὁ, ἡ δ., a slave;
__(a) fem., ἡ δ., a female slave, bondmaid (Cremer, 702; DB, iii, 215): Lc 1:38, 48 At 2:18" (LXX) ;
__(b) masc., ὁ δ., a slave, bond-man: Mt 8:9 18:23, al.; opposite to ἐλεύθερος, 1Co 7:22 12:13, Gl 3:28, Ef 6:8, Cl 3:11, Ap 6:15 13:16 19:18; opposite to κύριος, δεσπότης, οἰκοδεσπότης, Mt 10:24 13:27, 28 Lc 12:46, Jo 15:15, Ef 6:5, Cl 3:22 4:1, al.; metaphorically, δ. Χριστοῦ, τοῦ Χρ., Ἰησοῦ Χρ., Rm 1:1, 1Co 7:22, Gl 1:10, Ef 6:6, Fp 1:1, Cl 4:12, Tg 1:1, 2Pe 1:1, Ju 1; δ. τ. θεοῦ, τ. κυρίου, At 16:17, 2Tm 2:24, Tt 1:1, 1Pe 2:16, Ap 7:3 15:3; δ. πονηρός, ἀχρεῖος, κακός, Mt 18:32 24:48 25:26, 30, Lc 17:10 19:22; δ. ἁμαρτίας, Jo 8:34, Rm 6:17, 20; τ. φθορᾶς, 2Pe 2:19.
SYN.: διάκονος (q.V.), θεράπων, ὐπηρέτης (see DB, iii, 377; iv, 461, 469; DCG, i, 221; ii, 613; Cremer, 215, 702). (AS)

G1402.def:
δουλόω, -ῶ
(δοῦλος), [in LXX for עָבַד ;]
to enslave, bring into bondage: At 7:6 (LXX), 2Pe 2:19; metaphorically, 1Co 9:19; pass., before ἐν, 1Co 7:15; τ. θεῷ, Rm 6:22; τ. δικαιοσύνῃ, Rm 6:18; οἴνῳ, Tt 2:3; ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τ. κόσμου, Gl 4:3 (Cremer, 217).†
(AS)

G1403.def:
δοχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(δέχομαι), [in LXX: Gn 21:8, Et 1:3, al. (מִשְׁתֶּה), Dan LXX 5:1 (לֶחֶם) ;]
a feast, banquet: Lc 5:29 14:13.†
(AS)

G1404.def:
δράκων, -ο τος, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for תַּנִּין ;]
a dragon, a mythical monster: figuratively, of Satan, Ap 12:3-17 13:2, 4 13:11 16:13 20:2.†
(AS)

G1405.def:
δράσσομαι
[in LXX for נָשַׁק pi., Sl 2:12; elsewhere קָמַץ, as Lv 2:2 ;]
to grasp with the hand, to lay hold of: metaphorically, with accusative (M, Pr., 65), 1Co 3:19 (LXX).†
(AS)

G1406.def:
δραχμή, -ῆς, ἡ
(δράσσομαι), [in LXX: in Hex. for in בֶּקַע, שֶׁקֶל Ezra for אֲדַרְכֹּן, דַּרְכְּמוֹן ;]
a drachma, nearly equal to the Roman denarius (see: δηνόριον): Lc 15:8-9 (DCG, ii, 200).†
(AS)

G1407.def:
δρέπανον, -ου, τό
(later form of Attic δρεπάνη, δρέπω, to pluck), [in LXX for מַזְמֵדָה, חֶרְמֵשׁ, etc. ;]
a sickle, pruning-hook; Mc 4:29, Ap 14:14-19.†
(AS)

G1408.def:
δρόμος, -ου, ὁ
(δραμεῖν, see: τρέχω) [in LXX chiefly for מְרוּצָה ;]
a course: figuratively, of life or ministry, At 13:25 20:24, 2Tm 4:7.†
(AS)

G1409.def:
Δρούσιλλα (Rec. Δρουσίλλα), ης, ἡ
Drusilla, wife of Felix: At 24:24.†
(AS)

G1410.def:
δύναμαι, depon.,
[in LXX chiefly for יָכֹל ;]
to be able, have power, whether by personal ability, permission, or opportunity: with inf. (M, Pr., 205; WM, §44, 3) pres., Mt 6:24, Mc 2:7, Jo 3:2, 1Co 10:21, al.; with inf. aor., Mt 3:9, Mc 1:45, Jo 3:3, 4 Rm 8:39, al.; with accusative, to be able to do something: Mc 9:22, Lc 12:26; 2Co 13:8; absol., to be able, capable, powerful: 1Co 3:2 10:13.
(AS)

G1411.def:
δύναμις, -εως, ἡ
(δύναμαι), [in LXX for עֹז ,גּבוּרָה ,צָבָה ,(חֵיל) חַיִל, etc.; 35 words in all ;]
power, might, strength; relatively, ability, power to perform: Mt 25:15, At 3:12, Hb 11:11; κατὰ δ., 2Co 8:3; παρὰ δ., ib.; ὑπὲρ δ., 2Co 1:8; of pecuniary ability, 2Co 8:3, Ap 18:3; absol., power, might: Lc 24:49, At 1:8; opposite to ἀσθένεια, 1Co 15:43; ἡ δ. τ. ἁμαρτίας, 1Co 15:56; of power in action, Rm 1:16, 20 1Co 1:18, Fp 3:10, al.; ἡ δ. τ. θεοῦ, Mt 22:29, Mc 12:24, Rm 1:20, al.; opposite to μόρφωσις, 2Tm 3:5; in doxologies, Ap 4:11 7:12, al.; ἐν δ., Mc 9:1, Lc 4:36, Rm 1:4, al.; of the power of performing miracles, At 6:8, 2Ts 2:9; pl., Mt 13:54, Mc 6:14, Gl 3:5, al.; of the force or meaning of a word (Plat., al.), 1Co 14:11. By meton., of persons or things;
__(a) of God, Mt 26:64, Mc 14:62 (Dalman, Words, 200ff.);
__(b) of angels, Rm 8:38, Ef 1:21, 1Pe 3:22;
__(with) of armies, pl. [LXX for צְבָאוֹת ], metaphorically, of the stars, Mt 24:29, Mc 13:25, Lc 21:26;
__(d) of that wh. manifests God's power: Christ, 1Co 1:24; τ. εὐαγγέλλιον, Rm 1:16; ἡ δ. τ. κυρίου, 1Co 5:4;
__(e) of mighty works (Tr., Syn., §xci), δ. ποιεῖν, Mc 6:5 9:39; pl., Mt 7:22, Mc 6:2, Lc 10:13, al.; σημεῖακ. δ., At 8:13; δ. κ. τέρατα κ. σημεῖα, At 2:22, 2Co 12:12.
SYN.: βία, ἐνέργεια, ἐξουσία, ἰσχύς, κράτος (see Tr., l.with; Cremer, 218, 236; DB, i, 616; iv, 29; DCG, i, 607; ii, 188). (AS)

G1412.def:
δυναμόω, -ῶ
(δύναμις), [in LXX for עָזַז, Sl 52:7 68:28; גָּבַר pi., hi., Ec 10:10, Da TH 9:27 * ;]
to make strong, strengthen: Ef 6:10 (WH, mg.; ἐνδυν-, WH, txt., RV), Cl 1:11, Hb 11:34.†
(AS)

G1413.def:
δυνάστης, -ου, ὁ
(δύναμαι), [in LXX for גִּבּוֹר, עָרִיץ, בַּיִת, etc. ;]
a prince, ruler, potentate: Lc 1:52; of God (Sir.46:5, 16, 2Ma.15:3), 1Tm 6:15; of a high official (cf. δυνάσται Φαραώ, Gn 50:4), At 8:27 (Cremer, 221).†
(AS)

G1414.def:
δυνατέω, -ῶ
(δυνατός),
to be able, be powerful, mighty: with inf., Rm 14:4, 2Co 9:8; absol., opposite to ἀσθενῶ 2Co 13:3.†
(AS)

G1415.def:
δυνατός, -ή, -όν
(δύναμαι), [in LXX for גִּבּוֹר, חַיִל, etc. ;]
__1. strong, mighty, powerful: absol., Lc 1:49, 1 Cl 1:26; οἱ δ., the chief men, At 25:5 ; of spiritual strength, Rm 15:1, 2Co 12:10 13:9; before ἐν, Lc 24:19, At 7:22 18:24; πρός, 2Co 10:4.
__2. C. inf., able to do; Lc 14:31, At 11:17, Rm 4:21 11:23, 2Tm 1:12, Tt 1:9, Hb 11:19, Tg 3:2.
__3. Neut., δυνατόν, possible: Mt 19:26, Mc 9:23 10:27 14:36, Lc 18:27, At 2:24 20:16; εἰ δ. (ἐστι), Mt 24:24 26:30, Mc 13:22 14:35, Rm 12:18, Gl 4:15; τὸ δ. (= ἡ δύναμις) αὐτοῦ, Rm 9:22.†
(AS)

G1416.def:
δύνω Ion, and trag. form of δύω,
[in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא ;]
to enter, sink into; of the sun (sc. όντον), set: Mc 1:32, Lc 4:40
(cf. ἐκ-, ἀπ-εκ-, ἐν-, ἐπ-εν-, παρ-εισ-, ἐπι-δύνω).†
δύω, see: δύνω
δύνω Ion, and trag. form of δύω,
[in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא ;]
to enter, sink into; of the sun (sc. όντον), set: Mc 1:32, Lc 4:40
(cf. ἐκ-, ἀπ-εκ-, ἐν-, ἐπ-εν-, παρ-εισ-, ἐπι-δύνω).†
δύω, see: δύνω
(AS)

G1417.def:
δύο, numeral, indecl. exc. in dative, δυσί, δυσίν (Attic δυοῖν),
two: Mt 19:6, Mc 10:8, Jo 2:6, al.; with pl. noun, Mt 9:27 10:10, al.; οἱ, τῶν, τοὺς δ., Mt 19:5 20:24, Mc 10:8, Ef 2:15, al.; δ. ἐξ, Lc 24:13; distrib., ἀνὰ, κατὰ δ., two and two, two apiece: Lc 10:1 (WH, ἀνὰ δ. [δύο]), Jo 2:6, 1Co 14:27; δύο δύο (= ἀνὰ δ., as LXX, Gn 6:19 for שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם, but not merely "Hebraism," cf. μυρία μυρία, Æsch., Pers., 981, and for usage in π. and MGr., see M, Pr., 21, 97), Mc 6:7; εἰς δ. (two and two, Xen., Cyr., 7, 5, 17), into two parts, Mt 27:51, Mc 15:38.
(AS)

G1419.def:
δυσ-βάστακτος, -ον
(βαστάζω), [in LXX for נֵטֶל, Pv 27:3 * ;]
hard to be borne: Mt 23:4 (om. WH, txt., R, mg.), Lc 11:46.†
(AS)

G1420.def:
δυσεντερία, -ας, ἡ,
Rec. for δυσεντέριον (which see), At 28:8.†
(AS)

G1422.def:
δύσκολος, -ον
(κόλον, food), [in LXX for אֵיד, Jr 29:9 (Jr 49:8) (of. δυσκολία, Jó 34:30; εὔκολος, 2Rs 15:3) * ;]
__1. properly, of persons, hard to satisfy with food, hence, generally, hard to please (Eur., Plat.).
__2. Of things, difficult, hard (Arist.): Mc 10:24.†
(AS)

G1424.def:
δυσμή, -ῆς, ἡ
(= δύσις, δύνω), [in LXX for בּוֹא, עֲרָבָה, etc. ;]
mostly in pl., opposite to ἀνατολαί;
__1. a setting, as of the sun (accusative to Thayer, see word, so perhaps in Lc 12:54).
__2. the quarter of sunset, the west: anarth., Mt 8:11 24:27, Lc 12:54 13:29, Ap 21:13.†
(AS)

G1426.def:
δυσφημία, -ας, ἡ
(δύσφημος, slanderous), [in LXX: 1Ma.7:38, 3Ma.2:20 * ;]
evil-speaking, defamation: opposite to εὐφημία, 2Co 6:8.†
(AS)

G1427.def:
δώδεκα, οἱ, αἱ, τά indecl.
numeral, twelve: Mt 9:20 10:1, al.; οἱ δ., the apostles, Mt 10:5, Mc 4:10, al.; in At 19:7 24:11, for Rec. δεκαδύο.
(AS)

G1429.def:
δωδεκά-φυλος, -ον
(δώδεκα, φυλή),
of twelve tribes: as subst. neut., τό δ. (cf. λαὸς ὁ δ., Sibyll. Orac.), the twelve tribes, At 26:7.†
(AS)

G1430.def:
δῶμα, -τος, τό
(δέμω, to build), [in LXX for גָּג ;]
chiefly in poets and late (not Attic) prose;
__1. a house, hall.
__2. In LXX (and Hom., Od., x, 554; cf. MGr., terrace), house-top: ἐπὶ τ. δῶμα, Lc 5:19, At 10:9; ἐπὶ τ. δώματος, -άτων, Mt 10:27 24:17, Mc 13:15, Lc 12:3 17:31.†
(AS)

G1431.def:
δωρεά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(δίδωμι), [in LXX chiefly (-άν) for חִנָּם, as Gn 29:15 ;]
a gift: At 11:17, Rm 5:15, Hb 6:4; δ. τ. θεοῦ, Jo 4:10, At 8:20; τ. Χριστοῦ, Ef 4:7; τ. πνεύματος, At 2:38 10:45; τ. δικαιοσύνης, Rm 5:17; τ. χάριτος, Ef 3:7; ἀνεκδιηγήτὶῳ δ., 2Co 9:15. Acc, δωρεάν, adverbially (as frequently in LXX),
__(a) freely, as a gift: Mt 10:8, Rm 3:24, 2Co 11:7, 2Ts 3:8, Ap 21:6 22:17;
__(b) in vain, uselessly: (Jo 15:25 LXX) Gl 2:21.†
SYN.: see: δόμα (AS)

G1432.def:
δωρεάν, see: δωρεά.
δωρεά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(δίδωμι), [in LXX chiefly (-άν) for חִנָּם, as Gn 29:15 ;]
a gift: At 11:17, Rm 5:15, Hb 6:4; δ. τ. θεοῦ, Jo 4:10, At 8:20; τ. Χριστοῦ, Ef 4:7; τ. πνεύματος, At 2:38 10:45; τ. δικαιοσύνης, Rm 5:17; τ. χάριτος, Ef 3:7; ἀνεκδιηγήτὶῳ δ., 2Co 9:15. Acc, δωρεάν, adverbially (as frequently in LXX),
__(a) freely, as a gift: Mt 10:8, Rm 3:24, 2Co 11:7, 2Ts 3:8, Ap 21:6 22:17;
__(b) in vain, uselessly: (Jo 15:25 LXX) Gl 2:21.†
SYN.: see: δόμα (AS)

G1433.def:
δωρέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Gn 30:20 (זָבַד), Et 8:1, Pv 4:2 (נָתַן), Lv 7:15 (קׇרְבָּן), 1Es.1:7 Et 8:14 Et 8:55, Sir.7:25 * ;]
to present, bestow. As depon. (with same sense), -Ιομαι,.-οίμαι: Mc 15:45, 2Pe 1:3-4.†
SYN.: δίδωμι, q.v (AS)

G1434.def:
δώρημα, -τος, τό
(δωρέω), [in LXX: Sir.31:18 (Sir.34:18)* ;]
a gift, boon: Rm 5:16, Tg 1:17.†
SYN.: see: δόμα (AS)

G1435.def:
δῶρον, -ου, τό
(δίδωμι), [in LXX chiefly for קׇרְבָּן, also for מִנְחָה, etc. ;]
a gift, present: Mt 2:11, Ap 11:10; of gifts and sacrifices to God, Mt 5:23-24 8:4 15:5 23:18-19, Mc 7:11, Lc 21:1, 4, Hb 5:1 8:3-4 9:9 11:4; δ. θεοῦ, Ef 2:8.†
SYN.: see word δόμα (AS)

G1436.def:
ἔα,
interj.,
expressing surprise, indignation, fear (in cl. chiefly in poët.), ah! ha!: Lc 4:34.†
(AS)

G1437.def:
ἐάν, contr. fr. εἰ ἄν,
conditional particle,
representing something as "under certain circumstances actual or liable to happen," but not so definitely expected as in the case of εἰ with ind. (Bl., §65, 4; cf. Jo 13:17, 1Co 7:36), if haply, if;
__1. with subjc. (cl.);
__(a) pres.: Mt 6:22, Lc 10:6, Jo 7:17, Rm 2:25, 26 al.;
{ __(b) aor. (= Lat. fut. pf.): Mt 4:9 16:26 (cf. ptcp. in Lc 9:25; M, Pr., 230), Mc 3:24, Lc 14:34, Jo 5:43, Rm 7:2, al.; = cl. εἰ, with opt., Jo 9:22 11:57, At 9:2; as Heb. אִם = ὅταν, Jo 12:32 14:3, I Jo 2:28 3:2, Hb 3:7" (LXX) .
__2. C. indic, (as in late writers, fr. Arist. on; see WH, App., 171; VD, MGr. 2, App., §77; Deiss., BS, 201f., LAE, 155, 254; M, Pr., 168, 187; Bl., §65, 4);
__(a) fut.: Mt 18:19 T, Lc 19:40, At 7:7;
__(b) pres.: 1Ts 3:8 (see Milligan, in l.).
__3. With other particles: ἐ. καί (Bl., §65, 6), Gl 6:1; ἐ. μή (M, Pr., 185, 187; Bl., l.with), with subjc. pres., Mt 10:13, 1Co 8:8, Tg 2:17, 1Jo 3:21; aor., Mt 6:15, Mc 3:27, Jo 3:3, Rm 10:15, Gl 1:8 2:16 (see Lft., Ellic., in ll.); ἐ. τε . . . ἐ. τε, [in LXX for אִם . . . אִם, Et 19:13, al.,] Rm 14:8.
__4. = cl. ἄν (which see) after relat. pronouns and adverbs (Tdf., Pr., 96; WH, App., 173; M, Pr., 42f.; Bl., §26, 4; Mayser, 152f.; Deiss., BS, 202ff.): ὃς ἐ., Mt 5:19, Mc 6:22, 23 Lc 17:32, 1Co 6:18, al.; ὅπου ἐ., Mt 8:19; ὁσάκις ἐ., Ap 11:6; οὗ ἐ., 1Co 16:6; καθὸ ἐ., 2Co 8:12; ὅστις ἐ., Gl 5:10.
(AS)

G1438.def:
ἑαυτοῦ, -ῆς, -οῦ, dative -ῷ, etc., accusative -όν, etc., pi. -ῶν, etc. (Att. contr. αὑτοῦ, etc);
reflex pron.;
__1. prop, of 3rd person (Lat. sui, sibi, se), of himself, herself, itself, etc.: Mt 27:42, Mc 15:31, Lc 23:35, al.; added to a middle verb, διεμερίσαντο ἑαυτοῖς, Jo 19:24; to an active verb, At 14:14 (M, Pr., 157); ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ, Lc 12:57 21:30, Jo 5:19, al. (see: ἀπό); δι᾽ ἑαυτοῦ, Rm 14:14; ἐν ἑ., Mt 3:9, Mc 5:30, al.; εἰς ἑ., Lc 15:17; καθ᾽ ἑαυτόν, At 28:16, Tg 2:17; παρ᾽ ἑαυτῷ, at his own house, 1Co 16:2; πρὸς ἑ., with, to himself, Lc 18:11; as poss. pron. (with emphasis weakened; see M, Pr., 87f.), τ. ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς, Lc 9:60.
__2. As reflexive 1st and 2nd of person(s) (so also frequently in cl., chiefly poetry), Mt 23:31, Mc 9:50, Rm 8:23, 1Ts 2:8, al.
__3. In pl., for reciprocal pron., ἀλλήλων, -οις, -ους, of one another, etc.: Mt 21:38, Mc 16:3, Ef 5:19, al.
(AS)

G1439.def:
ἐάω, -ῶ,
[in LXX for רפה hi., etc. ;]
__1. to let, permit: with accusative, with inf., with accusative and inf. (M, Pr., 205): Mt 24:43, Lc 4:41 22:51, At 14:16; 16.7, 19:30 23.32 27:32 28:4 , 1Co 10:13.
__2. to let alone, leave: ἀγκύρας, At 27:40 (cf. προσ-εάω).
† (AS)

G1440.def:
ἑβδομήκοντα, οἱ, αἱ, τά, indecl.
(ἑπτά),
seventy: Lc 10:1, 17 At 7:14 23:23 27:37.†
(AS)

G1441.def:
ἑβδομηκοντάκις, adv.,
[in LXX for שִׁבְעִים, Gn 4:24 * ;]
seventy times: ἑ. ἑπτά, seventy times seven, Mt 18:22 (R, txt., ICC, in l.), or seventy-seven times (R, mg.; cf. M, Pr., 98; WM, 314; Meyer, in l.).†
(AS)

G1442.def:
ἕβδομος, -η, -ον
(ἑπτὰ), [in LXX chiefly for שְׁבִיעִי ;]
seventh: Jo 4:52, Hb 4:4" (LXX), Ju 14, Ap 8:1 10:7 11:15 16:17 21:20.†
(AS)

G1443.def:
Ἔβερ (Rec. Ἐβέρ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. עֵבֶר, Gn 10:24),
Eber (OT, Heber): Lc 3:35.†
(AS)

G1445.def:
Ἑβραῖος (WH, Ἐβ-), -α, -ον (Aram, עִבְרַי), as subst., ὁ Ἑ.,
[in LXX for עֵבֶר, עִבְרִי ;]
a Hebrew.
__1. In OT, of Israelites in contrast with those of another race (Gn 14:13, Êx 1:15, Dt 15:12, al.).
__2. In NT as the correlative of Ἑλληνιστής, a Jew who had adopted, in greater or less degree, Greek culture and Greek language. The distinction was not merely linguistic (DB, ii, 325); as far as it was so, Συριστής would be a more correct Greek term for the Jew of Semitic speech (see: Ἑβραΐς, and cf. Dalman, Words, 7): At 6:1, 2Co 11:22, Fp 3:5.
† (AS)

G1446.def:
Ἑβραΐς (WH, Ἐβ-), -ίδος (Aram. עִבְרַי), peculiar form of Ἑβραϊκός,
[in LXX, ἡ Ἑ. φωνή, 4Ma.12:7 16:15 * ;]
in NT, ἡ Ἑ. διάλεκτος, Hebrew, i.e. the Aramaic vernacular of Palestine: At 21:40 22:2 26:14.†
(AS)

G1447.def:
Ἑβραϊστί (WH, Ἐβ-), adv.,
[in LXX: Si prol. 13 * ;]
in Hebrew: Ap 9:11; elsewhere, in Aramaic (see supr.): Jo 5:2 19:13, 17, 20 20:16, Ap 16:16.†
(AS)

G1448.def:
ἐγγίζω (ἐγγύς).
[in LXX for נגשׁ, קרב, etc. ;]
__1. trans., to bring near: Gn 48:10, Is 5:8.
__2. Intrans., to come near: absol., Mt 26:46, Mc 14:42, Lc 18:40 19:41 21:20, 28 24:15, At 21:33 23:15; with adv., ὅπου, Lc 12:33; with dative, Lc 7:12 15:1, Luke.15.25 22:47, At 9:3 10:9 22:6; τ. θεῷ, Hb 7:19, Tg 4:8; before εἰς, Mt 21:1, Mc 11:1, Lc 18:35 19:29 24:28; πρός, with dative, Lc 19:37; μέχρι θανάτου, Fp 2:30; of time, ὥρα, Mt 26:45; ἡμέρα, Rm 13:12, Hb 10:25; καιρός, Mt 21:34, Lc 21:8; χρόνος, At 7:17; ἑορτή, Lc 22:1; παρουσία, Tg 5:8; τέλος, 1Pe 4:7; ἐρήμωσις, Lc 21:20; ἀπολύτρωσις, Lc 21:28; ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία (for similar expressions in Targ., see Dalman, 106), Mt 3:2 4:17 10:7 Mc 1:15, Lc 10:9 (ἐφ ̓ ὑμᾶς) 10:11 (cf. προσ-εγγίζω), and see Cremer, 224).
† (AS)

G1449.def:
1. to mark in or on, to paint on , (Herdotus Historicus)
2. to inscribe, write in or on , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., ἐγγεγραμμένος τι having something written on it, (Sophocles Tragicus); so Virgil flores inscripti nomina.

G1473.def:
ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
of person(s) pron.
I.
__(a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in Mt 3:11, Mc 1:8, Lc 3:16, al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as Mt 10:16, Jo 10:17; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. 1Rs 3:8), At 9:10; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, Jo 1:23 (LXX), At 7:32 (LXX).
__(b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, Jo 14:20; μου τ. λόγους, Mt 7:24; ὀπίσω μου, Mt 3:11; ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, Ap 5:5; also with the prep. πρός, as Mc 9:19, al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as Lc 10:16, Jo 7:23, Mc 14:7, al.
__(with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, Mt 2:6; μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, Mc 9:24.
__(d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, Jz 11:12, al.), i.e. what have we in common: Mt 8:29, Mc 1:24, 5:7, Lc 8:28, Jo 2:4; τί γάρ μοι, 1Co 5:2.
__(e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.).
__(f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: Mt 2:8, Lc 2:48, Jo 6:56, Rm 3:7, 1Co 7:40, al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, Jo 7:28.

G1487G.def:
εἰ,
conjunctive particle, used in conditions and in indirect questions.
__I. Conditional, if;
__1. with indic, expressing a general assumption;
__(a) pres.: before indic, pres., Mt 11:14, Rm 8:25, al.; before imperat., Mc 4:23 9:22, Jo 15:18, 1Co 7:9, al.; before fut. indic., Lc 16:31, Rm 8:11, al.; before pf. or aor., with negation in apodosis, Mt 12:26, Rm 4:14, al.; similarly, before impf., Lc 17:6, Jo 8:39; before quæst., Mt 6:23, Jo 5:47 7:23 8:46, 1Pe 2:20;
__(b) fut.: Mt 26:33, 1Pe 2:20;
__(with) pf.: Jo 11:12, Rm 6:5, al.;
__(d) aor.: Lc 16:11 19:8, Jo 13:32, 18:23, Ap 20:15, al.
__2. Where the assumption is certain = ἐπεί: Mt 12:28, Jo 7:4, Rm 5:17, al.
__3. Of an unfulfilled condition, with indic, impf., aor. or plpf., before ἄν, with imp. or aor. (see: ἄν, I, i).
__4. C. indic., after verbs denoting wonder, etc., sometimes, but not always, coupled with an element of doubt: Mc 15:44, 1Jo 3:13, al.
__5. C. indic., as in LXX (Nm 14:3o, 1Rs 14:45, al. = Heb. אִם), in oaths, with the formula of imprecation understood in a suppressed apodosis (WM, 627; Burton, §272): Mc 8:12, Hb 3:11" (LXX) 4:3 (LXX).
__6. Rarely (cl.) with optative, to express a merely possible condition: At 24:19 27:39, 1Co 14:10 15:37, I Pe3:14, 17.
__II. Interrogative, if, whether.
__1. As in cl., in indir. questions after verbs of seeing, asking, knowing, saying, etc.: with indic. pres., Mt 26:63, Mc 15:36, At 19:2, 2Co 13:5, al.; fut., Mc 3:2, At 8:22, al.; aor., Mc 15:44, 1Co 1:16, al.; with subjc. aor. (M, Pr., 194), Fp 3:12.
__2. As in LXX (= Heb. אִם and interrog. הֲ, Gn 17:17, al.; see WM, 639f.; Viteau, i, 22), in direct questions: Mc 8:23 (Tr., WH, txt.), Lc 13:23, 22:49, At 19:2, al.
__III. With other particles.
__1. εἰ ἄρα, εἴγε, εἰ δὲ μήγε, see: ἄρα, γε.
__2. εἰ δὲ καί, but if also: Lc 11:18; but even if, 1Co 4:7, 2Co 4:3 11:16.
__3. εἰ δὲ μή, but if not, but if otherwise: Mc 2:21, 22 Jo 14:2, Ap 2:5, al.
__4. εἰ καί, if even, if also, although: Mc 14:29, Lc 11:8, 1Co 7:21, 2Co 4:16, Fp 2:17, al.
__5. καὶ εἰ, even if, see: καί
__6. εἰ μή, if not, unless, except, but only: Mt 24:22, Mc 2:26 6:5, Jo 9:33, 1Co 7:17 (only), Gl 1:19 (cf. ἐὰν μή, 2:16; see Hort., Ja., xvi); ἐκτὸς εἰ μή, pleonastic (Bl., §65, 6), 1Co 14:5 15:2, 1Tm 5:19.
__7. εἰ μήν = cl. ἦ μήν (M, Pr., 46), in oaths, surely (Eze.33:27, al.): Hb 6:14.
__8. εἴ πως, if haply: At 27:12, Rm 1:10.
__9. εἴτε . . . εἴτε, whether . . . or; Rm 12:6-8, 1Co 3:22 13:8, al.
(AS)
